If you contributed camera trap data to WildObs, you will want to know what others now see:
which of your projects are listed, what their metadata say, when embargoed data will be
released, and how people will cite you. This vignette answers those questions with the same
public API key everyone uses. Here we use the package maintainer's projects as the example;
put your own name, email or ORCID in their place.


``` r
# load the R package
library(WildObsR)

# your personal API key, read from .Renviron (see the Get started vignette)
api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY")
```

## Find your projects

The `contributors` filter matches anyone listed on a project, in any role. Give a full name,
an email address or an ORCID; mixing them catches projects where you were listed
differently:


``` r
# query the database for projects listing this person, by name or ORCID
mine <- wildobs_mongo_query(api_key = api_key,
                            contributors = c("Zachary Amir", "0000-0002-8398-2059"))
# see which IDs were returned 
mine
#> [1] "QLD_Dwyers_Scrub_ANIM3018_2023_WildObsID_0005"
#> [2] "QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004"    
#> [3] "QLD_Kgari_potoroos_Amir_2022_WildObsID_0003"  
#> [4] "ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001"
```

## Check how your projects are described

The metadata contain the contextual information people should read first,
and the dataset's citation. You can download metadata alone, which
takes seconds, and check that the contributors, roles, organisations and licences are right:


``` r
# download the descriptors of your projects, without their tables
meta <- wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key, project_ids = mine, metadata_only = TRUE)
#> metadata_only = TRUE -> skipping data resource downloads for speed.

# extract the contributors table from the metadata 
contributors <- extract_metadata(meta, "contributors")
# and view who is credited on each project, and in what role
contributors[, c("title", "role", "DPID")]

#> 1       Zachary Amir principalInvestigator
#> 2      Annabel Smith          rightsHolder
```

You can read the same metadata without R on the
[WildObs Database Dashboard](https://dashboard.wildobs.org.au/camdb), where you created your
API key: each project's **More** button opens a summary of them. If any information is wrong,
missing, or you want to add new information, email <data@wildobs.org.au> and we will update
it, rather than you editing a download: the database is the record everyone else reads. This 
is mainly for metadata, but we can explore changes to the data tables too.

## Know when embargoed data are released

A project shared as `partial` lists its metadata but withholds its tables until its embargo
ends. The embargo runs for `embargoPeriodMonths` from the project's `created` date, and the
tables are released at the next database update after that:


``` r
# extract sharing preference and embargo length for each project
sharing <- extract_metadata(meta, "WildObsMetadata")
# gather the dates each project was created
created <- vapply(meta, function(dp) substr(dp$created, 1, 10), character(1))

# view the earliest date each embargo can end
data.frame(
  project = sharing$DPID,
  sharing = sharing$tabularSharingPreference,
  embargo_months = sharing$embargoPeriodMonths,
  # add embargo to created date to determine embargo release date 
  embargo_ends = as.Date(created[sharing$DPID]) + round(sharing$embargoPeriodMonths * 30.44),
  row.names = NULL
)
#>                                         project sharing embargo_months
#> 1 QLD_Dwyers_Scrub_ANIM3018_2023_WildObsID_0005    open              0
#> 2     QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004 partial             16
#> 3   QLD_Kgari_potoroos_Amir_2022_WildObsID_0003    open              0
#> 4     ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001    open              0
#>   embargo_ends
#> 1   2024-12-06
#> 2   2027-04-10
#> 3   2024-11-06
#> 4   2025-02-18
```

## See your data as others do

A public key returns your open projects exactly as anyone else receives them, which differs
from what you uploaded in three ways:

- **Threatened species are obscured** in the states where they are listed under the
  *Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999*. The species, date and
  count stay, but the camera identifiers are replaced, so no one can place the record.
- **Image file names are withheld**, and only images hosted openly by WildObs or the ALA 
  (`filePublic = TRUE`) can be downloaded.
- **Embargoed projects** show their metadata only, as above.


``` r
# download one of your open projects, as the public receives it
dp <- wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key,
                          project_ids = "ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001")[[1]]
# and pull out the observations table 
obs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations")

# subset obscured records that the public cannot place on a camera
obscured <- obs[grepl("^obscured_for_", obs$deploymentID), ]
# and view the threat category and species
table(obscured$scientificName, obscured$deploymentID)
#>                      
#>                       obscured_for_endangered_species
#>   Casuarius casuarius                             413
#>   Dasyurus maculatus                               39
```

Your own projects are the exception. Sign in to the
[WildObs Database Dashboard](https://dashboard.wildobs.org.au/camdb) with the email address
stored with your projects, and you can download each one in full from **My Datasets**:
unobscured, with file names, and whatever its embargo. WildObs emails you a secure link to
the data package as a .zip file. Unzip it and read it like any other data package, noting
that its times are in UTC, where `wildobs_dp_download()` gives local time:


``` r
# read your unzipped data package from the folder it was saved in
own <- frictionless::read_package(here::here("QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004",
                                             "datapackage.json"))
# then read its tables as usual
own_obs <- frictionless::read_resource(own, "observations")
```

## How you will be cited

Every project carries a citation that ties together each dataset's contributors, ending 
with its [RAiD](https://raid.org), a persistent identifier for your research activity. 
Anyone using `cite_datapackages()` receives it with the version of your data package they
downloaded, so you can search for your RAiD to find where your data were used:


``` r
# view citations from all projects with metadata
writeLines(cite_datapackages(meta))
#> Zachary Amir & Annabel Smith (2023). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: UQ's undergraduate widlife techonologies camera trapping module comparing human and AI comptuer vision [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/a3efd562. WildObs data package version 1.0.1.
#> Zachary Amir, Linda Behrendorff & Matthew Luskin (2022). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: UQ & QPWS collaboration to study impacts of 2019-20 bushfires on K'gari's long-nosed potoroos [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/ba8f4587. WildObs data package version 1.0.2.
#> Zachary Amir, Matthew Luskin & Linda Behrendorff (2023). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: Camera Trap Module for UQ's BIOL2015 Field Ecology Studies Course from 2023, 2024, 2025 [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/1b8c4374. WildObs data package version 2.1.1.
#> Zachary Amir, Tom Bruce & Matthew Luskin (2022). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: Zachary Amir's camera trap surveys from 6 national parks in QLD's Wet Tropics rainforests from late 2022 to early 2023 targeting feral and native vertebrates [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/cb5829ab. WildObs data package version 1.1.1.
```

Papers and datasets that are associated with a project are listed in its `relatedIdentifiers`:


``` r
# extract the related identifiers table from metadata
related <- extract_metadata(meta, "relatedIdentifiers")
# and view the type, ID, and the project it is from
related[related$relatedIdentifierType == "DOI", c("relationType", "relatedIdentifier", "DPID")]
#>      relationType                               relatedIdentifier
#> 6  IsSupplementTo              https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.71464
#> 8  IsSupplementTo https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2026.181926
#> 9      IsSourceOf                 https://doi.org/10.15468/kjqw3f
#> 10      IsCitedBy         https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19552244
#>                                         DPID
#> 6  ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
#> 8  ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
#> 9  ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
#> 10 ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
```

To add a publication that uses your data, please send its DOI to <data@wildobs.org.au>.
